title: Sidra's Best Buddy
markdown:
The moon, a giant pearl, was just peeking over the pointy tops of the Whisperwind Mountains. Sorrel, a young elf whose tunic matched the moss on the oldest trees, yawned and stretched his quick fingers. His little cottage near the sleepy ogre village was usually quiet at this hour: night crickets, the soft sigh of wind through pine. He hummed a tuneless melody, mind drifting to fluffy clouds and starlit streams.

A tiny tap-tap-tap at the door. Not the wind. Not a pinecone. A proper, hesitant knock. Sorrel opened it to find Sidra, a small ogre child, on the doorstep. The usual shy smile was gone. Big serious eyes, the colour of deep forest moss, looked sad, like a wilting flower after a hot day.

“Oh, Sidra,” Sorrel whispered, leaf-green tunic rustling. “What’s wrong, little one?”

Sidra shuffled large clumsy feet in the soft grass. “I need a pet, Sorrel,” pebbles rolling slowly. “But I don’t know which one. There are so many kinds, and they all seem so different.”

A thoughtful ogre child, usually quite sure. A pet was a very big decision. “Finding the right pet is a bit like finding the perfect mushroom after rain. It takes looking, and maybe a little adventure.” Warm as berry tea. “I’ll help you. Let’s walk in the moonlight and see what wonderful creatures we can discover.”

They set off, Sorrel’s light elven steps, pointed ears twitching, into moonlit fir woods. Cool air, sweet earthy pine, damp soil. Sidra walked beside him, large hands clasped. Shoulders slumped. Sorrel remembered how Sidra sometimes felt wobbly around the other ogre children, worried about stepping on a toe or knocking a stacked pile of stones with big kind hands. Perhaps not just a pet: a friend who wouldn’t mind clumsy ogre ways.

First, a patch of velvety moss where tiny glow-worms held a cheerful meeting, golden as scattered embers, chirps like fairy laughter. “Ooh, a visitor! You should have me as a pet! I can light up your whole room, no need for a lamp!”

Sidra watched the blinking lights. Pretty, like fallen stars, and very, very small. “They’re a bit blinky.”

“Perhaps a bit too much blink for a quiet companion.”

A little further, a babbling brook, water like scattered diamonds. On a smooth grey stone, a very large very green frog. “Ribbit! Looking for a companion? Excellent swimmers. Our nightly croaks are a lovely song of the pond. Think of the music!” Sidra eyed the wet gleam. Imagined splash and slippery skin. “I don’t think I can swim that well in a brook.” Hands wringing.

“Perhaps something a little less watery.”

They climbed a winding rocky path. High above, a fluffy mountain hare with twitchy whiskers nibbled tough grey moss, then hopped down, nose wiggling. “Hmph! Need a pet? I’m good at climbing. I can eat anything. You could have a pet that nibbles your boots!” Sidra actually giggled. “My boots are very tough.” A little smile. Then overwhelm: glow-worms too blinky, frog too wet, boots unappealing. Slumped on a conveniently placed rock.

“I don’t think I’ll ever find one.” A flutter. Sorrel put a comforting arm around those large shoulders.

The woods grew a little darker. A rustle in the bushes. Sidra clutched the tunic. Sorrel wanted to help find the friend who would make Sidra feel understood, but the frown was deeper than ever.

At the edge of the woods, an open meadow in silver moonlight. Sidra sat on cool dewy grass, head in hands. “It’s no use. I’m too clumsy for a tiny pet, and I don’t think a big one would like me very much. I guess I’ll just be lonely forever.”

Sorrel sat beside, grass tickling. “It’s not about being clumsy. It’s about finding someone who understands you. Someone who likes you just the way you are, clumsy hands and all.” He remembered Sidra once saying, in a rare burst of confidence, how the garden ladybugs and the quiet company of snails were a comfort. “What about a pet that likes quiet mornings and gentle hands? A pet that doesn’t mind a big warm ogre hug?”

Sidra looked up, a flicker of hope.

An idea like a sunbeam. “Come on! I think I know just the thing.”

They hurried toward Sidra’s cozy ogre cottage. From the garden, a soft rustling. Through the low wooden fence: nibbling bright green clover, a small fluffy creature with long soft ears and a wiggling nose. A mountain hare, like the grumpy one, but gentle and shy. It looked up, saw Sidra, and instead of grumbling or running, gave a soft twitch of greeting.

Sidra’s face lit like a harvest moon. Carefully through the gate. The hare hopped closer, sniffed an outstretched finger, then nudged the hand with a velvety nose.

“It likes me!” Kneeling, the little hare hopped onto a lap and snuggled. Usually clumsy hands were surprisingly gentle on downy fur. Happiness chased the worry. Instantly the name: Flicker.

Sorrel watched from the garden edge, a warm-blanket feeling. The moon, now high and bright, the same pearl that had peeked over the peaks, looked down on cottage, clover, and two quiet friends. Crickets hummed again. The door did not need another knock.
characters: Sidra (small ogre child), Flicker (a mountain hare)
